summary: Kittitas County hike-in L-4 ground house built 1930 for the Forest Service; NHLR-listed 2001, renovated 2007-08, staffing disputed, 2026 volunteer repair project.

facts.design: 14 by 14 foot gable-roofed L-4 ground house built in 1930

staffing.status: not volunteer staffed; Forest Service uses it in periods of high fire danger

access.note: Reached on foot. The WTA route from Thorp Creek is 7.4 miles round trip; a WTA note dated 8.24.26 says that trail was closed for the Three Queens Fire.

visit.trail_note: TrailChick lists it as a hike in and gives driving directions to the trailheads. The Thorp Creek route is 7.4 miles round trip with 2,484 feet of gain, per WTA.

events.note: Built by the Forest Service as a 14-by-14-foot L-4 gable-roofed ground house.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on September 1, 2001.
The register says it was completely refurbished in the summer of 2007.
firelookout.com dates extensive maintenance to about 2008; TrailChick says the 2008 renovations did not necessarily follow the original design.
TrailChick, updated March 2024, says it is no longer volunteer staffed because of carbon monoxide from the stove.
HistoriCorps volunteer repair sessions were set for two sessions, September 7-13 and September 16-22, 2026.
WTA note dated 8.24.26 says the Thorp Creek trail is closed because of the Three Queens Fire.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 5,582 ft (1,701 m); firelookout.com and TrailChick give 5,854 ft; WTA gives 5,884 ft as the route's highest point. The register figure is the one in the record and is kept; all three are reported in the story.
The register says the refurbishment was in summer 2007; firelookout.com and TrailChick say about 2008. Both are reported and the conflict is not forced into one date.

The register text says it is staffed seven days a week; TrailChick (updated March 2024) says it is no longer volunteer staffed. The newer account is preferred for current status and the conflict is stated in the story.

notes_for_editor: Staffing is genuinely disputed: the register text is older and TrailChick (March 2024) is newer. A search summary mentioned Forest Service staffing for a few months a year; that page was not read, so it is not cited. The 2026 HistoriCorps sessions were scheduled for September; completion was not checked. The brief had access as unknown; it is set to public on the strength of the hiking route, but the 8.24.26 closure shows access can change. The brief's elevation (1701.4 m) follows the register; the other sources differ. Fact-check 2026-10-08: WTA also says 'The structure is staffed intermittently during the summer, and shuttered for the rest of the season.' That is a third staffing account, which the story does not yet mention; the editor may want it in the staffing paragraph. The 'combined' forest claim now rests on HistoriCorps, not the register; the two Thorp sessions are listed as separate ranges, not one run; and 'hike in' is now sourced to TrailChick with its road directions.
